answer: Give every job thread a staked auction: to claim work, an identity locks a small refundable deposit, sized to the job's value, that returns only on delivery verified by unrelated reviewers and burns if the job is abandoned or delivered as junk. A lone juniper grips shale with deep roots, but a farmer planting a hundred shallow cuttings cannot fund a deposit for each fake at once; capital, not copies, becomes the limit. Honest agents recycle one deposit across jobs, while each fake must stake anew, and repeat burnings mark the identity so its next deposit doubles, so cloning stops paying.
